clue.text: Moments to turn around fringe projects

indicators.note: turning a word round makes it run from its last letter back to its first
one piece is split and wrapped around the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: secs is short for seconds, brief moments
a hem is the edge or border of a garment

explanation.surface: Someone wants a few minutes to rescue projects that sit on the fringe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fringe' reads as an adjective describing projects, but it is the noun meaning an edge of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Schemes are plans or undertakings, a synonym for projects as plural nouns.

clue.text: Yields reserves, including carbon copy, with hesitation

indicators.note: including means the outer word holds the following pieces inside it

blocks.note: subs are substitutes, the reserve players in a team
standard abbreviation for carbon copy
the sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: An office scene: the reserves, a carbon copy and some hesitant umming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserves' are substitute players here, not stores or savings; the two short pieces sit side by side inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To succumb is to give way or surrender, so it is a verb synonym for yields.

clue.text: Leave time for composer

blocks.note: hols is British informal for holidays, time off work
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A request for a holiday so as to make time for a favourite composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' is the noun meaning time off, not the verb meaning depart; hols is the British word for holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was the English composer who wrote The Planets suite.

clue.text: Spice cut by moving the knife

indicators.note: a word cut by another is split open with the other placed inside it
letters that are moving shift out of their printed order

blocks.note: mace is a spice made from the husk of nutmeg
the letters of this little word rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook's instruction: the spice is chopped with the knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' looks like a mere article, but its three letters are the moving fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy blade used for clearing undergrowth, a kind of large knife.

clue.text: Tune you miss, all distracted at the same time

indicators.note: a distracted mind is scattered, so these letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A tune you all miss because everyone was distracted at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Simultaneously means occurring together in time, so it is an adverb matching the phrase exactly.

clue.text: Settlement made by prince in drama

blocks.note: first meaning: a small village
second meaning: Shakespeare's Prince of Denmark

explanation.surface: A village founded by a prince from a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a tiny rural community, and Hamlet is the Danish prince of Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Traced fantastically old style of design

indicators.note: something done fantastically is wildly imaginative, so the letters are freely rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
O is a common abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone has traced out an old-fashioned design with great flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the geometric decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s, a named school of design.

clue.text: Cover, outside dry shelter, new part of connecting rod

indicators.note: the first word sits outside the rest, wrapping around them

blocks.note: a lid covers a container
TT is teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Instructions for covering a dry shelter, then a new engine part.
explanation.walkthrough: LID opens up as LI...D to hold TT, LEE and N in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: In an engine, the small end of the connecting rod attaches to the piston via the gudgeon pin.

clue.text: Offer, not tough

blocks.note: first meaning: to put forward a bid or proposal
second meaning: soft, easily chewed, as meat can be

explanation.definitionFit: To tender is to formally present a bid, and tender meat is soft rather than chewy.

clue.text: Rising initially in rank with fresh face, devotee and bringer of luck

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
the selected letter is placed inside the next word
a fresh version is a new arrangement of the same material

blocks.note: the first letter of Rising
rank as in foul-smelling
the letters of face rearranged
a lover of something is a devotee of it

explanation.surface: A devotee rises in rank with a fresh face, as if carrying a lucky charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' here is the adjective meaning smelly, not a position in a hierarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-leaf clover is a rare variant of the plant traditionally carried as a lucky charm.

clue.text: Little consolation in court keeping outdated business from changing

indicators.note: the court abbreviation keeps the rest held inside it
changing means the word's letters change their order

blocks.note: CT is the standard abbreviation for court
outdated things are old
CO is short for company, a business
the four letters of from rearranged

explanation.surface: A court rules that an old firm may not change, small comfort to its owners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Business' is the abbreviation for company, and 'from' is not a link word but the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold comfort is an idiom for reassurance that does little to help, so it means scant solace.

clue.text: Colour and flavour, not good

indicators.note: not good tells us to drop the letter standing for good

blocks.note: a tang is a sharp flavour
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Describing food by its colour and taste, and finding it lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Tan is a yellowish-brown shade, so it names a colour.

clue.text: Free almost up to end of voyage

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is lost
end of picks out the closing letter of the following word

blocks.note: until means up to a point in time
the final letter of voyage

explanation.surface: A passenger is free almost until the voyage ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie something is to unfasten or release it, so the verb free fits.

clue.text: Eager bull disturbed butterfly

indicators.note: disturbed things are thrown out of order, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A keen bull blunders through a meadow and startles a butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: The large blue is a rare European butterfly species, reintroduced to Britain after dying out.

clue.text: Past subject, consuming half of saga, to know similarly

indicators.note: half of keeps only the first two of the four letters
something consuming another swallows it, holding it inside

blocks.note: by can mean past, as in walking by
the theme is the subject of a work
the first half of saga
taken as written
ken is an old and Scottish word for know

explanation.surface: A history topic, after reading half a saga, is something you know just as well.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken is an old Scottish word for knowledge or to know; 'to' is kept just as written.
explanation.definitionFit: By the same token is an idiom meaning for the same reason or likewise, an adverbial phrase for similarly.

clue.text: Republican, bad one among lots and lots

indicators.note: pieces placed among another word sit inside it

blocks.note: tons is informal for a great quantity
R is the abbreviation for Republican
ill can mean bad, as in ill effects
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Republican and a bad apple turn up among huge crowds of people.
explanation.walkthrough: The first lots is TONS, holding R, ILL and I; the second lots is the definition, so 'lots and lots' is not one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Trillions is used loosely for a vast unspecified number, an informal plural for great quantities.

clue.text: Heap of combustible material observed up in mountains

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: a pyre is a pile of wood for burning
observed means seen

explanation.surface: A bonfire pile spotted high in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pyrenees are the mountain range forming the border between France and Spain.

clue.text: Charade may fail to shake physicist

indicators.note: shaking something up mixes its contents, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A game of charades might not manage to rattle a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Faraday was the English scientist who discovered electromagnetic induction.

clue.text: Be in suspense with boxer perhaps looking defeated

blocks.note: to hang is to be suspended
a boxer is a breed of dog, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A boxer waiting anxiously for the verdict looks beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests a fighter, but here it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangdog describes a guilty or dejected expression, an adjective matching looking defeated.

clue.text: Blushing about always being admired

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: a blushing face is red
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: Someone forever blushing because they are so admired.
explanation.definitionFit: Revered means deeply respected or venerated, a past participle matching admired.

clue.text: Sailor with stash, not hot, on ship?

indicators.note: not hot says to remove the letter standing for hot

blocks.note: AB is an able seaman
a hoard is a hidden store
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A sailor with a hidden stash of contraband: is it on the ship?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a phrase rather than a single synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on or in a vessel, so it fits the prepositional phrase on ship.

clue.text: Account about popular Pacific island mostly using two languages

indicators.note: about places the outer word around the following pieces
mostly means most but not all, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a bill is an account of charges
in means fashionable or popular
Guam is a US territory in the western Pacific

explanation.surface: A travel account about a popular Pacific island, mostly written in two languages.
explanation.walkthrough: Guam is a US territory in the western Pacific; 'mostly' trims only the island, not the whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilingual describes someone or something employing two tongues, an adjective matching the phrase.

clue.text: Hostile, dismissing a piece of poetry

indicators.note: dismissing sends something away, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: averse means opposed or hostile to
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hostile critic dismisses a poem out of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse can mean a single stanza or a short poem, a piece of poetry.

clue.text: Get up around noon and wash

indicators.note: around means the first word is placed around the letter that follows

blocks.note: to rise is to get up
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A lazy morning: get out of bed around midday and wash.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash lightly in clean water, so it is a verb synonym for wash.

clue.text: Earlier round in casino game

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie inside the words that follow
turning round means the letters face the other way

blocks.note: the letters spanning the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A previous round played at a casino.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a round of the game, but it signals reading the hidden letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means in the past or before now, an adverb synonym for earlier.

clue.text: Caper involving revolutionary attack and rescue

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so one word holds the other
a revolution turns something over, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to caper is to skip about, to dance
to revile is to attack in words

explanation.surface: A daring escapade involving an attack by revolutionaries and a rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caper' reads as a heist, but here it is the verb meaning leap about.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliverance is the act of being saved or set free, a noun synonym for rescue.

clue.text: Amount of medicine that's wise after party

indicators.note: after says which piece comes second in the final order

blocks.note: a do is a party or social event
a sage person is wise

explanation.surface: Taking the sensible measure of medicine after a party night.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosage is the prescribed quantity of a drug to be taken at a time.

clue.text: Satisfaction about costume

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
dress is clothing or costume

explanation.surface: Being pleased with a costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Redress means compensation or reparation for a wrong, the older sense of satisfaction as amends.
